start.whatP: Space Arenas is a deterministic, isometric real-time strategy game. You command a base, harvest supply from supply fields, generate power, train an army, and destroy every opponent's Command Center.
start.flow1: Command Center gives you power and can train Bulldozers.
start.flow2: Use a Bulldozer to build a Supply Dock (your income), then a Barracks for combat units.
start.flow3: Harvesters you build at a Supply Dock automatically ferry supply back for credits.
start.flow4: Watch your power — if production buildings need more power than plants provide, everything shuts down (buildings tint red with a lightning marker).
start.flow5: Attack-move your army at enemy bases. Win by destroying all enemy Command Centers.
start.matchP: In the Offline Game tab, pick a map, starting credits, and add bots at the difficulty you want. Assign every player a numbered Team (a 2-player map lists Team 1 and Team 2, a 4-player map Team 1–4). Players on the same team are allies: their units stay visible to you through the fog, friendly fire is off, and the team wins together when all other teams are eliminated. Each player also picks a Spawn — the numbered starting position shown on the map preview — so you can shuffle who starts where. Press Start Game; a 5-second countdown begins, then the match runs.
start.netP: Network rooms use the same build-a-match screen as offline: host a room with Create Game, then edit every player – and bot – name, team, spawn and difficulty before the match starts, exactly like the offline setup.
start.duringP: Open the Menu button (top-right) to pause and view live match stats, resume, or quit. When the match ends a results screen shows final stats for every team. Use Quit Game or the results Back to Menu button to return to the lobby and start a new match.

controls.inputIdleWorker: I or the Idle Worker button in the tool bar
controls.inputIdleDozer: D or the Idle Bulldozer button in the tool bar
controls.spawnPoint: Set spawn point (near the building; hold V)
controls.minimapJump: Jump to location / zoom from minimap
controls.inputEdgePan: Move the mouse to the screen edge while holding Ctrl
controls.right1: On a damaged or unfinished friendly building with a Bulldozer selected → build/repair it.
controls.right2: On a friendly Supply Dock with Harvesters selected → assign them to that dock.
controls.right4: On open ground with a production building selected → set its rally point.
controls.combatMove: Move — march to the spot; a selected group keeps formation and spreads out to avoid piling up.
controls.combatAttack: Attack — engage a selected enemy or point on the ground: if it is already in firing range the unit fires in place; otherwise it advances only to the edge of firing range, stops, and fires once — it never walks up to or past the target. Multiple units spread out around it.
controls.combatAttackMove: Attack-move (A + right-click) — advance along the path, engaging anything in range, but keep pressing toward the destination after each kill.
controls.combatKeepAttack: Keep attack (K + right-click) — like attack, but keeps pressing the spot and loops without stopping until you cancel.
controls.combatGuard: Guard (G + right-click) — units march to the guard position and form up around it, then act as turrets: they hold position and shoot anything that comes within firing range without ever chasing. Selecting a guard shows its range circle.

mobile.p: Turn on Mobile Mode with the toggle button in the lobby side menu (it remembers your choice). It adds touch controls and on-screen shortcut buttons so the whole game is playable without a mouse or keyboard.
mobile.inputBox: Turn on the X button, then drag with one finger
mobile.inputMove: With units selected, tap the target — an enemy is attacked, open ground moves your units, and tapping a friendly unit or building re-selects it (context-sensitive, like right-click on desktop)
mobile.inputCmdMode: Turn on the C button so every tap issues a command without the long-press (long-press still works as a fallback)
mobile.inputAttackMove: Turn on the A button, then tap
mobile.buttonsP: While in a match, Mobile Mode shows a small button column (bottom-left, above the event log):
mobile.bC: C — command mode: every tap moves (no long-press).
mobile.bX: X — toggles box select: drag to select multiple units.
mobile.bH: H — centers the camera on your home base.
mobile.bI: I — jumps to the nearest idle harvester (tap again to cycle to the next).
mobile.bD: D — jumps to the nearest idle bulldozer (tap again to cycle to the next).
mobile.shortcutsP: These are the keyboard shortcuts (B/P/F/M/H/I/D/S/L/X and hold-A) as tappable toggles.
mobile.toolbarNote: Mobile Mode also keeps a fixed tool bar at the right of the screen (Satellite, Idle Worker, Idle Bulldozer), and a Deselect button appears next to Destroy so you can clear your selection.

units.p: Infantry are cheap and fast; vehicles are tougher and hit harder. Bulldozers build and repair; Harvesters gather supply automatically once a dock exists. Infantry train at the Barracks, vehicles at the War Factory.
units.ghostP: Units hidden in the fog still show a faint centered marker, so you can spot activity even when the unit details are hidden.

buildings.p: Every finished building that consumes power (barracks, docks, factories, turrets, tech centers) stops working if your team's power net drops below zero.

power.p1: Each team has a power budget: generation (Command Center +10, each Power Plant +50) minus usage from finished buildings. If usage exceeds generation, the whole team powers down:
power.l3: Power-using buildings are tinted red and show a lightning marker above them.
power.p2: Power status is live: the moment you finish a new Power Plant, buildings and the power bar recover automatically.
power.maxPowerP: A finished Power Plant at full health can be pushed to Max Power from its command bar: power generation is doubled for {s} seconds. When the overdrive ends the plant overheats and its health drops to 50% — a damaged plant cannot be overdriven until a Bulldozer repairs it back to full.
power.s1: Supply fields are solid deposits on the map; each has a capacity shown by its bar and trips/capacity label.
power.s2: A Harvester built at a Supply Dock automatically picks the nearest field, loads, returns, and grants $50 per trip.
power.s3: Fields deplete; when one is empty harvesters switch to another. The map has small corner fields that refill gameplay pacing, and mid fields.
power.s4: Oil fields can be claimed: keep a Scout inside one and after a short claim time it starts paying your team $50 every 10 seconds. A bar above the field shows claim / income progress.
power.s5: Oil fields stay captured once claimed and cannot be stolen — the first team to park a Scout there keeps the income for good.

bots.p: Bots share the same build order logic but differ in how fast they plan, how much economy they run, and how aggressively they attack. Lower difficulty = slower, more passive, weaker economy. Higher difficulty = denser base, faster planning, more frequent attacks.
bots.prose: • {difficulty} — plans every {interval}; keeps ${reserve} in reserve (floor ${floor}); runs up to {harvesterCap} harvesters with {dozers} dozer(s); reinforces its army once it has {army} combat units and launches an attack roughly every {attackInterval}; keeps {powerMargin} spare power capacity. Builds: {targets}. Produces: {products}.
bots.deterministic: Every bot is deterministic: on the same seed and settings it always takes the same actions, so matches are reproducible.

tech.p: Radar connects your minimap — until it is researched the minimap is offline and shows only a "CONNECT RADAR" notice. Satellite (requires Radar) scans the whole battlefield, briefly revealing every unit and building even in fog; use the Satellite button in the top-right tool bar, then wait for its cooldown. Select a Tech Center and press the Research button to start research.

role.bulldozer: Builds and repairs your base and buildings.
role.harvester: Gathers supply from fields and banks credits.
role.scout: Fast, long-vision recon that reveals the map, spots enemy movement, and claims oil fields.

role.fighter: Ghost fighter: flies over anything, strikes once, then returns to the Air Force to reload.
